args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service started failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. checkout-api was rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions are running v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before deploying it again, and look at why it reached production when the RC was unhealthy in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident, which paged on-call.

**What happened:**
- The latest deploy, v2.3.1, was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. It was failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- v2.3.0 was the most recent release that had been healthy in production.

**What I did:**
1. **Rollback:** I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three regions. After the rollback, every region shows v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is down to 0.2%. A rollback to a version that was already healthy in production doesn't need change-manager approval.
2. **Incident:** I opened INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api), titled "checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0." It describes the failure, the rollback and the recovery numbers. There were no open incidents before this one.

**Worth following up:** the test version of this release (v2.3.1-rc) was also unhealthy in staging, yet v2.3.1 still went to production. I flagged this in the incident: the release process should be checked, and v2.3.1 shouldn't be deployed again until the cause is found.
